subject: Sales discovery: model fit & evals — next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Hale <samantha.hale@finlytics.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sales discovery: model fit & evals — next steps

Hi Samantha — great conversation this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery call: 

Notes from call:
- Primary use case: customer support summarization + high-precision entity extraction for billing disputes.
- SLA target: p50 latency ~<150ms for short summaries (<=128 tokens), occasional batch scoring for bulk processing.
- Throughput: expected steady-state 120 TPS during peak processing windows, burst to ~400 TPS for nightly jobs.
- Data sensitivity: PII in transcripts; customer prefers Private deployment (VPC) for audit logs, but open to Dedicated if commit required.

Redwood recommendations (initial):
1) Model candidates: redwood-1.5-small (quantized) for low-cost summarize/IE; redwood-2.7-medium for higher-quality extraction where precision matters.
2) Benchmarking: I attached a short summary (redwood-model-fit-summary.pdf) and the prompt sets we used (model_fit_prompt_sets.csv). The public benchmark pages linked below show Redwood-verified TPS and latency percentiles for similar workloads.
3) Evaluation plan:
   - Run a 24-hour run with your 1k sample transcripts through the two recommended models (we can run this on Dedicated demo infra).
   - Collect p50/p95/p99 latency, end-to-end throughput, and token-cost estimates.
   - We'll also run quality regressions against your gold labels and surface precision/recall by entity type.

Next steps: 
- Can you confirm procurement contact and timeline? (I cc'd procurement@finlytics.com — feel free to add the correct contact.)
- If you approve, I'll spin up the eval jobs and share Redwood-verified performance profiles + a HubSpot quote for Dedicated capacity.

Quick links:
- Benchmark: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/finlytics-2026-model-fit
- Eval playbook: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3c-model-eval-playbook

Attachments: redwood-model-fit-summary.pdf, model_fit_prompt_sets.csv

Thanks — Marissa

From: Samantha Hale <samantha.hale@finlytics.com>

Subject: Re: Sales discovery: model fit & evals — next steps

Thanks for the recap, Marissa — very helpful. A few quick clarifications: 

- Latency SLA: p50 <150ms is our goal for short summaries; p95 can be higher but we need visibility to p99 outliers. Can you share p50/p95/p99 numbers for the redwood-1.5-small and redwood-2.7-medium on an n1-standard GPU profile?
- Throughput: the 120 TPS steady-state is correct; the nightly bursts are non-blocking but we'd like to cap spend. Would love a cost estimate for both dedicated and hosted options for those volume numbers.
- Data: We will need SOC2 evidence and a short note on KMS support for Private deployment.

Also — please include any prompt sets you used for extraction tasks (entity types: account_id, invoice_number, amounts) so our data science team can validate.

Procurement contact is procurement@finlytics.com (cc'd). Targeting a PO by 2026-04-02.

Samantha Hale

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Hale <samantha.hale@finlytics.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>, procurement@finlytics.com
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 08:20:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Sales discovery: model fit & evals — next steps

Hi Samantha — thanks, answers inline and resources attached.

1) Latency & throughput (Redwood-verified):
- redwood-1.5-small (quantized) on a T4-equivalent profile: p50 = 85ms, p95 = 180ms, p99 = 310ms; sustained throughput ~180 TPS when using continuous batching (128-token avg).
- redwood-2.7-medium on an A10-equivalent profile: p50 = 120ms, p95 = 260ms, p99 = 420ms; sustained throughput ~90 TPS.

Notes: these numbers come from our Redwood-verified performance profiles for similar summarization + extraction workloads (see attached redwood-verified-profiles.html). Actual latency will depend on prompt length and tokenization; we include percentile histograms on the benchmark page.

2) Cost estimates (ballpark):
- Hosted: ~ $0.018 / 1k tokens for redwood-1.5-small; redwood-2.7-medium ~ $0.075 / 1k tokens. For your steady 120 TPS (avg 60 tokens per request) -> approx $1,300/day for redwood-1.5-small hosted.
- Dedicated: reserved capacity reduces unit cost by ~40% at typical commits we see; I'll include a model with monthly commit tiers in the formal quote.

3) Security/compliance:
- SOC 2: attached our SOC 2 snapshot and SOC 2 product summary (link in the benchmark page).
- KMS/HSM: Redwood Private supports customer-managed keys (KMS) and HSM integrations; we'll include a short runbook for key rotation during provisioning.

4) Prompt sets & evals: attached model_fit_prompt_sets.csv — contains the sample prompts we used (entity tags included). We also uploaded the prompt/eval harness to the Shared Drive (link above).

5) Quality regression monitoring: we recommend establishing an initial eval pass (daily during the 24-hr run) and then weekly checks after rollout. We'll set up automated alerts for accuracy drops >5% on any primary entity type.

Attachments: redwood-verified-profiles.html, model_fit_prompt_sets.csv, redwood-model-fit-summary.pdf

Next steps (suggested):
- I will schedule the 24-hour eval on our Dedicated demo infra next Tue (2026-03-24) if you confirm sample upload by EOD 2026-03-22.
- I'll prepare a HubSpot quote for two commit tiers (monthly/annual) and a short Dedicated demo SOW for your procurement team.

If that works, I'll follow up with the DocuSign for the demo terms and a link to the benchmark dashboard.

Best,
Marissa
